table.title: [val] Code · CLI flags
table.md:
| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--max-old-space-size` | number | `4096` | Sets the max memory size of V8's old memory section, in megabytes. |
| `--experimental-vm-modules` | boolean | `false` | Enables experimental ES module support in the `vm` module. |
| `-r`, `--require` | string | — | Preloads the specified module at startup. |
| `--inspect-brk=[host:]port` | string | `127.0.0.1:9229` | Activates inspector and breaks before user code starts. |

understanding.purpose: Document CLI flags, their value types, defaults, and effects.
understanding.reading: Readers scan flag names to find an option, then compare its type and default before reading its description. On a phone, the initial viewport should make identification easy while keeping the cost of scrolling to explanations reasonable.
groups: Flag and Description identify each option and explain what it does.
Type and Default describe the value accepted and the behavior when the flag is omitted.
keep_intact: Flag identifiers and their punctuation, especially long option names and placeholders.
Type names and default values, including the address and port.
may_wrap: Descriptions can wrap at word boundaries.
The short and long aliases in a Flag cell can wrap between aliases; existing row height from descriptions can absorb some wrapping.

preferred.name: r2A
preferred.note: Keep r1C's intact flag identifiers and restore the wider description from r1A and r1B. This should reduce description wrapping at the cost of additional horizontal scrolling.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Give flag names more room while retaining a moderately narrow Description column; test whether fewer flag breaks improve row rhythm enough to justify the extra scroll.

acceptable.name: r1C
acceptable.note: Keep flag cells on one line and use the compact description width, testing whether easier identification is worth the wider initial scroll.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Test an intermediate Flag width to reduce identifier wrapping while bringing more of Default into the initial viewport. Retain the wider Description column for comfortable reading after scrolling.

acceptable.name: r2C
acceptable.note: Keep flags intact while giving Description more room than r1C, with less total scrolling than the intact-flags option. This tests whether a modest description increase improves the row rhythm.

acceptable.name: r3A
acceptable.note: Retain enough Flag width for the longest cell on one line and use the narrower Description width to reduce scrolling. Check this render against r2C, whose visible column proportions appear inconsistent with its stated widths.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Trim Flag modestly from r2A while keeping Type, Default and Description unchanged. Test whether aliases can wrap without splitting identifiers and whether the recovered viewport space improves access to Default.

acceptable.name: r3C
acceptable.note: Keep identifiers, types and defaults intact while narrowing Description further. This tests whether a small increase in description wrapping is a worthwhile reduction in horizontal scrolling.

bad.name: contrast
bad.note: This fits the viewport, but forces breaks inside long flags and the default address. The narrow description column would also produce many short lines, making each row harder to scan.
bad.why: This fits the viewport, but forces breaks inside long flags and the default address. The narrow description column would also produce many short lines, making each row harder to scan.

rationale: r2A keeps the flag names and default values intact while giving descriptions enough width to stay within three lines. Its horizontal overflow is substantial, but the first view still establishes the flag, type, and part of the default column; readers must scroll to compare descriptions. The shorter r1B reduces scrolling but wraps several flags, making identifiers harder to recognize as units.

general: Preserve identifiers and values as readable units when readers need to recognize or copy them.
Judge horizontal scrolling against the cost of narrow columns, fragmented text, and tall rows.
Give descriptive prose enough width for natural line breaks while keeping short categorical columns compact.
specific: The flag and default columns need substantial width to keep this table's code-like values intact.
A description width of 210px keeps the tallest cell to three lines in r2A.

tradeoffs: A designer could prefer r1B for its smaller scroll distance, accepting wrapped flags, or r3A for a modest reduction in width while retaining the same reported row heights.
uncertain: The reported widths for r2C and r3A are identical, but their supplied screenshots appear different; their comparison should be checked against the original renders. The ranges are approximate and should be verified in the browser.

critique.good: The generous Flag and Description columns preserve identifiers and make each explanation easy to read, with a consistent two-line rhythm.
critique.problems: The table requires substantial horizontal scrolling to reach the descriptions; much of the flag width is unused on shorter entries.
critique.cause: Flag at 225px accommodates the longest cell on one line, while Description at 300px adds considerably to the total width.

critique.good: Type and Default remain intact, and the narrower Flag column reduces scrolling while allowing aliases to wrap. Descriptions retain a comfortable measure.
critique.problems: The first two rows grow taller and the explanation column still lies largely beyond the initial viewport.
critique.cause: Flag at 140px introduces wrapping, and the 260px Description column keeps the overall table wide.

critique.good: This is the most compact option without reported mid-word splits. The initial viewport presents Flag, Type, and most of Default together.
critique.problems: Descriptions are comparatively narrow, creating a taller, less even rhythm. The longest flag entries wrap, and the end of the address falls just beyond the viewport.
critique.cause: The 127px Flag and 180px Description widths save horizontal space but create additional lines; the first three columns total 338px before the table border.

critique.good: The compact Flag column brings Type and Default into the initial viewport, with the start of Description also visible. The descriptions have enough width to keep the rows relatively compact.
critique.problems: Long flag identifiers fragment across two or three lines, making them harder to find and copy accurately. Description still requires horizontal scrolling.
critique.cause: At 127px, Flag has only 106px for text, so the browser wraps identifiers at punctuation. The 210px Description column extends well beyond the viewport.

critique.good: Flag names have more breathing room than in r1A, while Type and most of Default remain visible initially. The wider Flag column does not increase row heights.
critique.problems: Several identifiers still break across lines, including the address placeholder. The description is entirely off-screen, and the longest default reaches beyond the viewport edge.
critique.cause: The 160px Flag column is wider but still too narrow for the longest complete identifiers. Its extra width shifts Default and Description to the right.

critique.good: Complete flag identifiers stay on one line and are easy to scan. Type remains visible alongside them.
critique.problems: The viewport cuts through Default, hiding part of the address and leaving Description entirely off-screen. The first data row is noticeably taller, producing more empty space beside its flag.
critique.cause: The 225px Flag column accommodates the longest one-line content but pushes the other columns right. The 180px Description column wraps its text more heavily than the 210px version.

critique.good: Flag identifiers remain intact and are easy to scan. Type and Default form a compact pair, while the description width supports readable wrapping.
critique.problems: The initial viewport cuts through the Default column and leaves Description off-screen. Readers must scroll substantially to read each explanation.
critique.cause: The 225px Flag column preserves even the longest cell on one line, but it pushes the 135px Default column beyond the viewport; the 210px Description column adds to the total scroll distance.

critique.good: The narrower Flag column brings more of Default into the initial viewport and reduces horizontal scrolling. Type remains compact and descriptions retain the same width as in r2A.
critique.problems: Long flag identifiers split across lines, making the option names harder to recognize and copy. The address still extends beyond the initial viewport.
critique.cause: At 190px, Flag has only 169px of text space, less than the width needed for the longest identifiers. The combined widths of Flag, Type and Default still exceed the viewport.

critique.good: The rendered initial view shows Type and the complete Default values, with the beginning of Description visible. This makes value comparisons convenient.
critique.problems: Several flag identifiers fragment across multiple lines, weakening the scan path and making the rows visually uneven. The render appears inconsistent with the stated 225px Flag width, so its actual width should be checked before drawing conclusions from the supplied dimensions.
critique.cause: The visible Flag column is too narrow to hold the identifiers intact; a 195px Description column also requires more wrapping than the 210px version.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

contrast.why: The flags and types are easy to scan, but the default is cut off at the viewport edge and the description requires scrolling. The tall rows also leave substantial empty space in the visible columns.

r1B.why: Several flags wrap, the long default reaches beyond the viewport, and the description is entirely offscreen. The resulting rows are tall despite the limited information visible at first.

ref_equal.why: All four columns fit, but the narrow widths split flags, the address, the Description header, and ordinary words. The fragmented text makes both scanning and comparison difficult.

ref_auto.why: The full default column fits and the description begins in view, but flags wrap heavily and the narrow description creates very tall rows. Most description text still requires scrolling.

r2A.why: The first flag stays intact, but two longer flags wrap and the long default is cut off. The description remains offscreen, though the visible rows are relatively compact.

r1C.why: All flags and types are intact and easy to compare, with compact, consistent rows. The long default is cut off and descriptions require horizontal scrolling.

raw.unsure: The supplied images do not show the full offscreen table for several layouts, so I cannot reliably compare their description widths or the full cost of scrolling.

ref_equal.why: Everything fits in the viewport, but flag names, the address, the Description header and prose split awkwardly across many lines. The resulting rows are difficult to scan.

r1B.why: Type and Default are readable at first sight, but several flags wrap and the Description column lies beyond the visible area, requiring horizontal scrolling.

contrast.why: The flags stay intact and are easy to scan, though the wider first column pushes part of Default and all of Description beyond the viewport.

r2A.why: The first flag stays intact, but longer flags wrap and the address extends beyond the viewport. Description requires scrolling.

r1C.why: The flags stay intact and the rows are compact. The tradeoff is that part of Default and all of Description require horizontal scrolling.

ref_auto.why: Some Description text appears at the viewport edge, but too little to read comfortably; several flag names also wrap. The default address remains intact.

raw.unsure: The supplied images do not show the full width of the horizontally scrolling layouts, so I cannot judge the complete Description columns or the total scrolling distance. C and E appear close; E's more compact rows suggest a more generous Description column.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
